sections.h2: Which office files Kalamazoo County land records?
sections.html:
Land records for Kalamazoo County are kept by the Register of Deeds in the County Administration Building, 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49007, phone 269-383-8970. The county calls the register of deeds a constitutional office dating from 1835, and says recording makes a document public without making it legally valid.

Staff index and preserve the records. Title searches and legal advice are off limits to them. In most sales a title company makes the trip or e-records the deed. A seller filing alone should read the checklist below, since the counter turns away papers that miss a formatting rule.

Kalamazoo County has four cities (Galesburg, Kalamazoo, Parchment and Portage) and five villages (Augusta, Climax, Richland, Schoolcraft and Vicksburg), according to Wikipedia. All of them record at this single office.

sections.h2: What does filing a document cost at the Kalamazoo County counter?
sections.html:
The county fee schedule sets recording at $30 a document under MCL 600.2567. A few extras can apply:

  • $3 more for each added instrument on a paper that assigns or discharges several.
  • Copies at $1 a page, plus $5 a document if certified.
  • $5 per search when staff look something up.
  • A $5 treasurer certificate for up to 20 tax ID numbers on one document, and 20 cents for each description after that.

The counter takes cash, checks, money orders and cards. Recording checks go to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, and certificate checks to the treasurer involved. No online pay portal exists for counter filings, so card payers phone the office or come in. The full list is on the county fee schedule.

sections.h2: How do Kalamazoo County sellers calculate transfer tax?
sections.html:
The seller's transfer tax is paid at the counter when the deed goes on record. The schedule gives $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied to a price rounded up to the next $500, so $100,000.01 becomes $100,500.

Those amounts are the statutory 55 cents and $3.75 per $500 restated per thousand. The county rate sits in MCL 207.504, and the state act names the seller as the person who owes the tax in MCL 207.523.

The middle row starts from the Census median value of $241,800 and rounds up to $242,000. A chart on the county website covers other prices, and the site links exemption lists for both taxes.

sections.h2: Which Kalamazoo County deeds need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
If the grantor "warrants" or "defends" the title in the deed, the treasurer must clear taxes first. The county's list names warranty and covenant deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments with warranty wording, and master deeds, including amendments that add property to a condominium. The rule comes from MCL 211.135.

A house inside the City of Kalamazoo adds a step. The seller gets a city certificate from the City Treasurer at Kalamazoo City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036, for $10, and the County Treasurer issues its own only after that.

A parcel with unpaid taxes cannot be cleared until the balance is paid at closing. Request a payoff figure early, because interest builds monthly on delinquent balances.

sections.h2: What must a paper show to be accepted in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
Layout is governed by MCL 565.201, and the county FAQ restates it as a checklist:

  • White copy paper, letter or legal size.
  • Black ink, 10 point type or larger.
  • A clear 2.5 inch strip across the top of page one, the document type printed on the first line below it, and half inch margins elsewhere.
  • A notary for the deed types the county lists, including warranty, quitclaim, executor, trustee and sheriff's deeds. Witnesses are no longer required.
  • Court documents bearing the court's certification and seal.

A rejected paper returns with a letter stating why, and you correct and refile it. Adding or removing a name on a deed takes a new deed, and the office cannot draft one, so use an attorney or title agency.

sections.h2: Can I record a Kalamazoo County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, through four certified vendors, which are Simplifile, Indecomm, ePN and CSC. Filings are processed on county business days, payment moves by ACH under each vendor's agreement, and vendors may add their own processing fees. Plats and master deeds with full size maps cannot be sent this way.

Michigan's statewide e-recording standards took effect on January 1, 2014, and the county follows them. Sellers rarely meet a vendor, because the title company submits the deed.

A Consumer E-Recording portal serves one time filers with affidavits, discharges, mortgages, certificates of trust, liens and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are excluded, so a seller recording a deed should use the counter or a title company.

sections.h2: How do I search Kalamazoo County land records?
sections.html:
The Document Searches page on kalcounty.gov is the starting point. Its Deeds Search tool costs nothing for index searching, then $1 a page plus a processing fee to view, print or save an image. Tapestry EON, available since October 21, 2024, costs $8.75 per search, and Laredo is a monthly subscription aimed at frequent users like title professionals.

Staff can fetch your latest deed for $5 a property and $1 a page, with certification at another $5. Public workstations in the Administration Building let you search grantor and grantee names free, charging $1 a printed page. Name searches beat address searches, since recorded papers need no address.

Land record images reach back to 1831, though the complete index only starts in 1984. A title company search is the safer route for a long chain of title.

sections.h2: What happens to a Kalamazoo County deed when an owner dies?
sections.html:
Surviving owners do not need a new deed, the county says. Recording an official death certificate with this office shows the deceased owner's interest has ended, and the certificate becomes part of the title chain. Photocopies of death certificates are refused.

Heirs who plan to sell should ask the title company what authority it needs, because county staff cannot advise on that. A free fraud alert is also offered. Enter a personal or business name and you are told whenever a matching document is recorded, which helps protect an empty inherited house.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Kalamazoo County housing?
sections.html:
Renters take a bigger share here than in Jackson or Kalkaska counties, so many sellers are landlords. QuickFacts reports 263,795 residents in mid 2025, 116,117 housing units, and owners living in 64.5 percent of occupied homes for 2020 to 2024.

  • Middle home value: $241,800.
  • Household income, midpoint: $72,532 in 2024 dollars.
  • Gross rent, midpoint: $1,093 monthly.
  • Adults 25 and over holding a bachelor's degree: 41.3 percent.

Wikipedia lists 562 square miles of land, with I-94 crossing the middle of the county and US 131 through its west central part. Owners outside the city limits record here too but ask a township or village treasurer about local tax.

faqs.q: What is the price of getting a deed on record in Kalamazoo County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document. Transfer tax and treasurer certificates are billed separately, and a paper discharging several instruments adds $3 per extra one.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax my bill as a Kalamazoo County seller?
faqs.a: Yes, the seller does, at the Register of Deeds counter when the deed is recorded. The county charges $1.10 and the state $7.50 for every $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Does a house in the city of Kalamazoo need two tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. A parcel within city limits pays $10 for the city certificate first, then $5 for the county one.

faqs.q: Are witnesses required on a Kalamazoo County deed?
faqs.a: No. A notary is the requirement now, for warranty, quitclaim and most other deed types.

faqs.q: May I use a card for Kalamazoo County recording fees?
faqs.a: Yes, by calling the office at 269-383-8970 or paying at the counter at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue. The county has no online payment portal for counter recordings.
